To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the pairwise estimation method can be used to infer the Granger-causal relations in a system of WSS processes, (2) the pairwise estimation is more accurate than the pairwise Granger-causability test, (3) the pairwise estimation can be applied to systems of processes with non-Gaussian distributions and (4) the pairwise estimation may be useful for the inference of Granger-causal structures in systems of WSS processes.

i) for a family of jointly WSS processes, pairwise methods can be used for inferring causal structures in the network; ii) the accuracy of such methods is affected by both the number of observations and the degree of correlation between the processes; iii) the accuracy of the pairwise methods increases with the number of observations; and iv) the performance of the methods is improved by using a larger number of lags.

(i) pairwise Granger-causalty tests may be used to infer the interdependence structure of large systems; (ii) the performance of pairwise Granger-causal inference is affected by the correlation structure of the system and by the choice of the time window; (iii) for systems that are not strongly correlated, a large time window is recommended.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods to infer causal relations in complex networks of WSS stochastic processes from a finite set (or a few) of observations.
the development and application of a novel approach to inferring causal relations among a set of jointly WSS processes by means of pairwise Granger-causalty tests.

the following issues: (i) to develop methods to identify pairwise causal relations between a family of processes, (ii) to determine whether these methods are able to identify all causal relations between the processes, (iii) to develop an efficient algorithm to compute the pairwise causal relations between processes and (iv) to investigate the performance of the methods in the presence of noise and to determine their sensitivity to noise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of a large number of variables, it is more efficient to first investigate the pairwise relationships and then to combine the results in order to infer causality in the system.
, in the absence of a priori knowledge, pairwise methods are a good first step in determining the interdependence structure of complex systems.
, while pairwise methods are not capable of providing the complete picture, they are useful and reasonably accurate tools for inferring causal relations in complex systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed pairwise estimation methods can provide a useful and reasonably accurate approximation to the full system structure.
the pairwise methods can be used to identify causal relations in a network of WSS processes, and they can also be used to estimate the strength of these causal relations.
pairwise Granger-causal relations can be reliably inferred from a finite set observations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of pairwise Granger-causation estimation methods can be a useful tool for inferring causal structures in complex networks of stochastic processes.
pairwise estimation methods can be a viable option in the case where the full system is too complex to handle.
pairwise methods are a viable alternative to more complicated and computationally demanding techniques for large networks.
